description: Canonical catalog for generated event/schema/id/operation registry views.

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for standard ck.* Event.kind values and wire scopes.

generated_registries.name: schemas
generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for active schema IDs and schema file locations.

generated_registries.name: id_kinds
generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for ck:<kind>: typed ID prefixes and storage/wire rules.

generated_registries.name: operations
generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for service operation IDs across HTTP, gRPC, and MQ surfaces.

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for canonical capability action vocabulary, risk tiers, required constraints, and event_kind targets.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

registry_rules: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a Move effect or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Anchor frontier, Move state_root, or reducer state.
Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into a shared Realm Move/Anchor history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable ck.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any Move has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, anchorer, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by Move preconditions/effects, Anchor DAG finality, and per-cell Lattice join. Compatibility Event Envelope fields are payload routing only and MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ck.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Realm official or sponsoring organization statement

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ck.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).

Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the compliance-floor escape switch
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.
Circle patch (ck.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-anchor commits opaque sub_anchor_head_digest to the Realm Anchor stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ck.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ck.profile.update patch semantics.

Flow business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Flow.stage / Flow.stage_changed_at; ck.flow.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=flow_already_terminal; state=archived yields flow_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Flow tracks patch. payload.patch uses ck.patch.v1 against the Flow.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Flow move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, flow_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->flow_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source.
Flow reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ck.flow.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update).

Set or clear a per-(flow, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (flow_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ck.flow.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> flow) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ck.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/flow-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ck:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Flows MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Flows MUST be relocated before)
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ck.morph.schema.migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, expires_at, and approval_evidence.
Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, revoked_at, revoked_by, and revocation_frontier.

Agent signing key rotation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_rotate_payload; key_id names the retiring key and replacement_key_id names the new key under the same accountable_principal_id with equivalent or narrower agent_key_scope.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state (CXP-0008 §4.11). Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within the revocation freshness window. Reversible via ck.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active (CXP-0008 §4.11). Reducer MUST re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state (CXP-0008 §4.11). MUST fan-out ck.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ck.capability.revoke for all active grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal (CXP-0008 §4.8). Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ck.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request (CXP-0008 §4.8). Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request (CXP-0008 §4.8.1). Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request (CXP-0008 §4.8.1). Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ck.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Realm-scoped profile override. The event kind keeps the historical space_override spelling for wire compatibility; payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_class.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_did context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ck.audit.release; ck.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ck.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref.
Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent anchor backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.
Lift a previously anchored moderation decision

Submit an appeal against an existing ck.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal flow).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ck.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal after the decided window expires (default 30 days). Transitions cell state decided → closed; locks against re-appeal of the same target by the same appellant. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ck.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

schemas.description: Circle — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Subset membership, independent history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity or policy server. Introduced by CXP-0007; see zh/models/circle.md.
Reference business-field schema used by the Morph type-system example. It validates the customer_risk fields.status / fields.severity payload carried inside ck.schema.morph.v1 containers.
Closed response DTO bundle for authorization query operations.
Registered schema for the embedded ck.patch.v1 field-patch wire format.
Closed request DTO bundle for realtime media service operations.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for account self-service operations: viewer, register, profile update, and session revocation.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for Blob service operations.
Signed principal-control record selecting the active backup series for one (actor_id, backup_class).
Canonical plaintext keybag opened from a ck.schema.key_backup.v1 envelope.
Proof binding a key-backup read/decrypt action to one recovery session, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and accepted proof transcript.

Wire payload schema for the principal recovery policy. Bound to the Principal Control Realm via signed publish / rotate / share-revoke; receivers MUST reject recovery / rotate / ck.device.authorize and cross-signing-reset evidence whose proof family is not allowed by the currently accepted recovery policy. See identity/key-management.md §3.3 / §7 / §8.

Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine, including create/get session shape, proof submit/complete request and response helpers, and principal_signing recovery proof transcript. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Signed completion receipt for a principal recovery flow. Bound to recovery_session_id used by every proof, backup unlock, and MLS Welcome replay during the recovery. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 step 7.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for push device registration and push wakeup delivery.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, and push webhook registration operations.
Signed DID continuity / migration proof payload
Encrypted minimal-metadata binding from Realm-scoped pairwise DID to principal DID, scoped by realm_id and trust_domain.
Realm-scoped member display/subject projection carried by ck.member.identity.update; handle lifecycle is carried by ck.schema.handle_claim.v1.
Directory response listing currently visible handle claims for a disclosed subject DID.
Builder-side candidate object for Handle resolution intent=member_add | invite (identity-handles.md §3.7); produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after Join Policy re-validation.

Time-bounded routing hint returned by Realm discovery / resolve paths for selecting a qualified service to receive join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join submissions. Not an authorization grant and not a member_delivery_binding.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for MIMI provider interop operations.
Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.applet.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.
Controller-signed package used by ck.applet.install preview/commit to derive ck.applet.registration and capability grants. Distribution object only; not Realm history truth and not authorization.
Canonical Applet InstallPlan returned by ck.applet.install.preview and recomputed by ck.applet.install before commit. plan_digest is calculated over this object with plan_digest omitted.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for ck.applet.install.preview and ck.applet.install.
Schema-registry object for agent protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.agent.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.
Signed hard-erasure receipt payload for ck.audit.erasure_receipt
Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_digest
Wire payload schema for ck.cross_signing.publish — establishes the PSK→{SSK, USK} binding on the principal control stream. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.
Wire payload schema for ck.cross_signing.reset — retires the current (SSK, USK) generation under one of four kinds of high-risk proof. See device-lifecycle.md §14.1.
Anchor DAG finality commitment schema
Closed request/response DTO bundle for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for Applet edge and bridge operations.
Structured Bottom (⊥) diagnostic surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined
Closed request/response DTO bundle for ck.keys.keypackages.upload, claim, consume, and revoke.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for ck.keys.upload, query, claim, and key backup put/list/delete responses.

Canonical ServiceDescribe response for ck.server.describe and per-surface describe operations: base service metadata plus claim-level partitions (supported_operations / implemented_features / claimed_profiles / verified_profiles / experimental_features / compat_surfaces). Enforces development_mode=true => verified_profiles=[]. compat_surfaces is limited to external interop surfaces. See service-surface.md §3.0.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from ck:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Anchor hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ck.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ck.component.moderation_appeal.v1 cell. Created by ck.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent protocol session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `ck.agent.protocol_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `ck.agent.session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}` (frozen wire_compat_grandfather bridge — see capabilities.md §5.0 and renames.json migration_group `wire_compat_grandfather`). The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `ck:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ck.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ck.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ck.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery flows to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CXP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `ck.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ck:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ck.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery flow. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Cokret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter parameter set, same response shape). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.events.query binding (Events/Query / events.query), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.events.query for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CXP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Flow lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Space lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity.

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; bio migrates to profile_fields.bio and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.events.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (events.subscribe = per-Realm event log; account.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Replaces the prior Matrix-derived long-poll ck.account.sync; not wire-compatible with Matrix /sync.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance to-device ack, account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ck.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ck.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories. wire_compat_grandfather entries MUST declare grandfathered_since.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ck.audit.accessed pair (same model as ck.flow.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ck.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="flow_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.wire_compat_grandfather: Legacy action/event naming divergence retained for wire compatibility; new entries are forbidden.
